test_policy.notes: Freshman applicants may apply test-optional (some applicants are required to submit scores). International applicants follow the test-flexible policy: only proof of English proficiency is needed, and SAT/ACT scores are not mandatory (they may be submitted, and an SAT EBRW of 520+ or ACT composite of 19+ also proves English proficiency).

requirements.notes: Apply with the Common App or the Suffolk application. International first-year applicants submit an essay/personal statement, an official secondary transcript in English (Suffolk may require a NACES credential evaluation at the applicant's cost), one letter of recommendation, and one official English proficiency score report. The $50 fee is the IPEDS 2024-25 figure (the admissions pages do not print the amount) and is waived when the applicant visits in person or virtually.

deadlines.label: Early Action, fall admission (fall 2027 entry)
deadlines.notes: Dates are printed without a year; taken as the fall 2027 cycle.

deadlines.label: Fall priority application date (fall 2027 entry)
deadlines.notes: Fall admission is rolling after the priority date ('Rolling: Ongoing'). Spring admission has a Nov. 15 priority date.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Exempt if from a country where English is the first and official language; also accepted: IB HL English predicted score, IGCSE/GCSE first-language English or AS/A-level results, a B average in AP English Language and Composition or Literature and Composition, or a Gaokao interview. TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, MET and PTE scores must be sent by the testing agency. Students who do not yet meet direct-entry requirements can enter through INTO Suffolk programs (Academic English, International Direct, International Year One), which give a degree-seeking I-20 and full admission on completion.

english.notes: Home Edition and TOEFL iTP China accepted; TOEFL Essentials minimum 8.5 also accepted. School code 3771. No 1-6 scale minimum is published.
IELTS One Skill Retake is also considered.
PTE Academic. Michigan English Test (MET) minimum 58 is also accepted.

cost.notes: Undergraduate resident (on-campus) estimate for 2026-27: tuition $51,340, fees $656, housing $19,962, food $5,900, books $1,200, loan fees $74, transportation $1,334, miscellaneous $1,994 (total $82,460). One tuition rate for all students.

aid.notes: All applicants are automatically considered for merit aid; Suffolk's merit scholarships for international students cover up to 50 percent of tuition (no dollar range or GPA grid is published). Need-based financial aid is available to U.S. citizens and permanent residents only.

ielts.note: No code listed; scores are sent by the testing agency.

duolingo.note: No code listed; scores are sent through Duolingo.

pte.note: No code listed; scores are sent by Pearson.

tier_notes.general: Editorial judgment: an 82% admit rate (fall 2024) with SAT section medians of 620 EBRW / 590 Math among the 12% who submit, and a Boston campus, place it just above the open-access D tier.
